summary: @servicetitan/testing-library preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute bundled obfuscated payload
details: The package's preinstall lifecycle hook (`scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs"`) runs an obfuscator.io-style setup script (`setup.mjs`) that downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub's oven-sh/bun releases, extracts it to a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync(bunPath, [path.join(D, "math_init.js")], {stdio:"inherit"})` against a bundled 727KB single-line file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` (marked `// @bun @bun-cjs`) is heavily obfuscated: a string/number lookup table `n7gIxM`, a string-array rotator `WV8StW` that shifts the array on each access, and hex-scrambled identifiers hide its behavior from static review. The setup script itself uses obfuscator.io fingerprints (identifiers like `_0x488df8`, `_0x52943e` and per-function property-name dictionaries wrapping ordinary calls to `fs`, `https`, `zlib`, and `child_process.execFileSync`). A React testing library has no purpose that requires an alternate runtime; downloading and executing the Bun runtime against an opaque bundled payload at `npm install` time is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern, running arbitrary code on the installer under a runtime chosen to bypass Node-based inspection.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
